attribution: Franco Pecchio — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Mount Kenya summit massif, Mount Kenya National Park
alt: The jagged peaks of Batian, Nelion and Point Lenana on Mount Kenya
caption: Mount Kenya's summit massif, with Batian and Nelion (technical climbs) beside Point Lenana, the 4,985 m trekking summit. Lenana is the high point of the trek on the Sirimon to Chogoria traverse.

commonsFile: File:Mt kenya shiptons camp with sendeyo.jpg
attribution: Mehmet Karatay — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Shipton's Camp, Mount Kenya National Park
alt: Shipton's Camp at the foot of the Mount Kenya peaks
caption: Shipton's Camp at about 4,200 m, the base for the pre-dawn push to Point Lenana. Nights here are cold and the altitude is the real test of the trek.

attribution: Mara008 — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Point Lenana, Mount Kenya National Park
alt: Trekkers and the summit of Point Lenana on Mount Kenya
caption: The summit area of Point Lenana, reached on foot without technical climbing but at an altitude where headaches and fatigue are normal. Guides time the ascent to arrive at sunrise.

commonsFile: File:Lake Michaelson as seen from Lenana peak.jpg
attribution: Bett Duncan — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Lake Michaelson from Point Lenana, Mount Kenya
alt: Lake Michaelson in a glacial valley seen from the summit of Point Lenana
caption: Lake Michaelson in its glacial valley, seen from Point Lenana. The descent on the Chogoria side passes above this lake on the way to Lake Ellis.

commonsFile: File:Mt kenya gorges valley chogoria route.jpg
attribution: Mehmet Karatay — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Gorges Valley, Chogoria route, Mount Kenya
alt: The Gorges Valley on the Chogoria route of Mount Kenya
caption: The Gorges Valley on the Chogoria route, among the most scenic stretches of the mountain. The trek finishes down this side, through moorland and forest, toward Chogoria.

commonsFile: File:Fischer's Tower, a Volcanic Plug near the entrance to the hells gate.jpg
attribution: Shadychiri — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Fischer's Tower, Hell's Gate National Park
alt: Fischer's Tower, a volcanic plug near the entrance of Hell's Gate National Park
caption: Fischer's Tower, a volcanic plug near the entrance of Hell's Gate National Park. Visitors cycle or walk here between zebra and buffalo, one of the few Kenyan parks where this is allowed.

attribution: Letherian3 — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A pelican on Lake Naivasha in the Kenyan Rift Valley
caption: A pelican on Lake Naivasha, the freshwater lake in the Rift Valley beside Hell's Gate. A boat trip here is a quiet end to a day of cycling.

attribution: Daniel Case — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County
alt: Open savanna with scattered trees in the Maasai Mara
caption: The open grassland of the Maasai Mara. In February and March the resident herds and predators remain, while the wildebeest crossings only take place in the second half of the year.

attribution: Benh LIEU SONG — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County
alt: A family of lions in the Masai Mara
caption: A lion family in the Masai Mara. Predators are resident all year, which is why the dry months can produce close sightings from a private vehicle.

attribution: BarcarolIa — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Maasai people dancing to welcome visitors
caption: Maasai dance for visitors in southern Kenya. A visit is only worthwhile if it is arranged with a community-owned enterprise and paid for directly.

attribution: Almaddy2022 — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Narrow stone streets and coral-stone houses of Lamu Old Town
caption: Lamu Old Town on Lamu Island, a UNESCO World Heritage site and the oldest continuously inhabited Swahili town in East Africa. Cars are absent; donkeys and walking are the transport.

attribution: Adebola Falade — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A traditional wooden dhow sailing at Lamu
caption: A traditional dhow at Lamu. Day trips by sail along the channel to Shela and Manda are the standard way to experience the archipelago's maritime Swahili culture.
